finding.claim: GET /users returns the id and name of every user in whichever org the caller names. The org comes from the query string, and the file shows no authentication or tenant check. Any caller can enumerate users of any organization (cross-tenant IDOR). It is a candidate only: an auth middleware outside this file could mitigate it, and req.pg is also set by middleware outside this file.
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1") with the result returned via res.json(rows)

trace.note: Route is registered with no auth or authorization middleware
req.query.org is used directly as the tenant filter with no comparison against the caller's own org
Matching rows are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The query is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. I found no app.use() middleware in the file, no session or user check, and no comparison of the requested org with the caller's org. req.pg is set outside this file, and I could not check whether that middleware enforces auth or tenancy.

verdict.guard_found: none (only the parameterized $1 placeholder at db.js:9, which prevents SQL injection but not cross-tenant access)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth or tenant check and queries by attacker-supplied req.query.org. db.js is the only file in the directory and `app` is neither exported nor given any app.use(), so no outside auth middleware can apply to it. Caveat: nothing in this directory sets req.pg, so the handler throws as written unless a DB is injected some other way.
